run_metadata.coverage_summary: Degraded run due to an outbound network-policy (egress) restriction. WebSearch (Anthropic search infrastructure) was available and was used to query across all three tiers: Tier 1 government portals (AusTender, buy.nsw / NSW eTendering, Buying for Victoria, QTenders / Queensland Supplier Portal, Tenders WA, SA Tenders and Contracts, Tenders Tasmania, NT QTOL, ACT Tenders), Tier 2 (VendorPanel public tenders, Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, NBN Co, Australian universities incl. Sydney/Melbourne/UWA) and Tier 3 corporate/construction (SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery, BHP Find Opportunities, Rio Tinto Buy Local, Fortescue, EstimateOne). However, EVERY attempt to open a buyer/detail/listing page — via WebFetch and via Bash curl — returned an egress-proxy denial (CONNECT tunnel failed, HTTP 403) for all external hosts (e.g. tenders.gov.au, tenders.nsw.gov.au, tenders.vic.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au, estimateone.com, bhp.com, and third-party listing sites). Because no tender detail page could be opened and verified, and because WebSearch's synthesised prose proved unreliable this run (one candidate it asserted, Wingecarribee Shire Council 'RFT T-2026-14' for the Moss Vale Aquatic Centre heating upgrade, could not be corroborated on cross-search — the only real Wingecarribee heating tender found, ref 6330/12.25, is ARCHIVED not current), no opportunities were captured as confirmed tenders. Per the routine's strict no-fabrication / fidelity rule, unverifiable search-synthesised specifics (IDs, closing dates, values) were deliberately NOT recorded rather than guessed. Tier 3 was checked as mandated: no publicly-visible Australian corporate RFx could be confirmed (the known corporate portals are login-gated and were unreachable to open this run). This run therefore records zero tenders and zero new sources, with the blockage documented in gaps.
gaps: OUTBOUND EGRESS BLOCKED: this session's network policy denied CONNECT to all external tender hosts at the agent proxy (HTTP 403 'CONNECT tunnel failed'). Confirmed via /root/.ccr/README.md: a proxy 403 means the destination host is not allowed by the organisation's egress policy for this session; the guidance is to report, not retry or route around. WebFetch and Bash curl were both affected identically.

Tier 1 government portals unreachable to open/verify (all returned proxy 403): www.tenders.gov.au (AusTender), www.tenders.nsw.gov.au / suppliers.buy.nsw.gov.au, www.tenders.vic.gov.au, qtenders.hpw.qld.gov.au / supply.qld.gov.au, www.tenders.wa.gov.au, tenders.sa.gov.au, www.tenders.tas.gov.au, tendersonline.nt.gov.au (QTOL), www.tenders.act.gov.au. RSS/API endpoints (e.g. tenders.nsw.gov.au RSS, tenders.gov.au atm.xml) were blocked identically.
Tier 2 unreachable to open/verify: vendorpanel.com.au public tenders, sydneywater.com.au, melbournewater.com.au, nbnco.com.au, and university procurement portals.

Tier 3 unreachable to open/verify (login-gated AND egress-blocked this run): service.ariba.com Discovery, bhp.com/suppliers, riotintobuylocal.onlineprocurement.com.au, fortescue supplier centre, estimateone.com. No publicly-visible corporate RFx could be confirmed; none fabricated.

WebSearch (the only working retrieval path) returns synthesised summaries that could not be cross-verified against source pages this run and produced at least one non-corroborated specific (Wingecarribee 'T-2026-14'); such unverified specifics were excluded rather than recorded.
Because no detail pages could be opened, no deliverables/requirements extraction was possible this run.

Note (not a tender): the ADF Health Services procurement (Department of Defence, potential replacement of incumbent provider) surfaced in search as live but is a restricted RFT released only to shortlisted organisations (invitation-only) — out of scope by the routine's rules and therefore not recorded as a tender.
